title: Why can't Indian job seekers tell a real job offer from a scam?
summary: Almost every Indian job seeker now sees fake offers, and half can't tell a real recruiter from a scammer. Here's "OfferCheck", a job-offer verifier one person could build with Claude in a weekend.
who: Freshers, Gen Z candidates and people switching jobs after layoffs, who get offers by WhatsApp, Telegram and email that ask for fees, bank details or ID documents. Genuine employers and HR teams also lose good candidates who now ignore real outreach out of fear.
facts: **Where this came from:** Recent Indian surveys by Indeed and LinkedIn, police and cyber-safety advisories covered by The Week and Free Press Journal, and many recurring job-seeker threads on Indian career subreddits such as r/developersIndia describing fee-based fake offers.

**Exposure is near-universal.** 93% of Indian workers surveyed by Indeed (1,161 respondents) have met suspicious or fraudulent job opportunities, and 51% are not confident they can tell a genuine recruiter from a scammer ([CXOToday](https://cxotoday.com/research/indeed-report-job-scams-erode-trust-as-50-of-indian-job-seekers-struggle-to-spot-real-recruiters/)).

**Fear also blocks real hiring.** At least 75% sometimes or often ignore opportunities they fear are fake, and 14% say they missed genuine opportunities because of that caution ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/jobs/story/more-than-9-in-10-job-seekers-encounter-fake-job-offers-542006-2026-07-09)).

**Scammers follow one pattern.** LinkedIn says 90% of reported scam attempts try to move the chat to personal messaging apps, often in the first message, and 82% of Indian professionals now check for fraud before applying ([People Matters](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/talent-management/82percent-indian-professionals-now-check-if-jobs-are-scams-before-applying-linkedin-49585)).

**The stakes go beyond lost fees.** A Patiala police case cited in an Asia Pacific money-laundering report found fake remote-job recruiters collecting bank accounts and SIM cards, with about Rs 2.99 crore moved through 18 mule accounts ([The Week](https://www.theweek.in/news/sci-tech/2026/08/04/new-cyber-scam-warning-your-job-application-could-make-you-a-money-mule.html)).
players: Job platforms protect their own pages: LinkedIn has added recruiter, company and job-listing verification and ID checks for higher-risk posters ([People Matters](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/talent-management/82percent-indian-professionals-now-check-if-jobs-are-scams-before-applying-linkedin-49585)). The government's CyberDost advisories and the 1930 helpline cover awareness and reporting ([The Week](https://www.theweek.in/news/sci-tech/2026/08/04/new-cyber-scam-warning-your-job-application-could-make-you-a-money-mule.html)). The gap is the offer that arrives off-platform, on WhatsApp or personal email, where nobody checks it before the candidate pays or shares documents.
pitch: "OfferCheck" lets a candidate forward any job offer, message or PDF and get a clear verdict in a minute: likely genuine, needs checking, or likely scam, with the reasons and the safe next step.
features: Paste text, forward a WhatsApp message or upload an offer letter PDF or screenshot.
Flags fees, deposits, requests for bank details or OTPs, moves to personal chat apps, and salary far above the market.
Compares the sender's email domain and website with the company's official domain, and checks domain age.
Writes a polite verification email to the company's official HR address and a report text for the cyber crime portal.
Lets genuine companies list their real recruiter emails and domains, so candidates can confirm outreach in one click.
capabilities: Builds the web app and WhatsApp bot, the domain-lookup service, tests and deployment.
Reads the offer text or PDF, extracts company, sender, salary and asks, and explains the verdict in plain English or Hindi.
A "job-scam-red-flags" skill holds the checklist from CyberDost advisories and known scam patterns, so every check is consistent.
Quick clickable prototype of the check and verdict screens to show candidates and college placement cells.
Gmail connector during development to test against real forwarded offers (with consent).
A daily job that collects new scam patterns from news and police advisories and proposes updates to the red-flag skill.
plan: Collect 30 real job messages (genuine and fake) from friends and placement cells, anonymised. Label each one.
Write the red-flag checklist as a Claude skill and test it against the 30 labelled messages.
Ask Claude for an artifact of the paste-and-check screen and show it to five job seekers.
Use Claude Code to build the Next.js app with text, PDF and screenshot upload.
Add email-domain versus official-domain matching and domain-age lookup.
Add the verification email and cyber-crime report drafts.
Add a WhatsApp number where candidates forward a message and get the verdict back.
Share with two college placement cells and one job-seeker community, and measure accuracy on new messages.
prompt:
Build a mobile-first Next.js + TypeScript web app called "OfferCheck" for Indian job seekers.

Flow: the user pastes a job message, or uploads a PDF or screenshot -> the server extracts text (OCR for images) -> call the Claude API to extract company name, sender email/phone, role, salary, and any requests (fees, deposits, bank details, Aadhaar, OTP, moving to WhatsApp/Telegram) as JSON -> run checks: sender email domain vs the company's official website domain, domain age via WHOIS, salary vs a simple role-band table -> combine into a verdict (Likely genuine / Needs checking / Likely scam) with a list of reasons -> show the verdict, the reasons in plain English, and two drafted texts: a verification email to official HR and a cyber-crime report.

Include: a red-flag rules file I can edit, 30 sample messages as test fixtures with expected verdicts, a test that reports accuracy, no storage of uploads beyond 24 hours, and a clear note that the result is guidance, not a guarantee.
pricing: Free for job seekers: unlimited checks.
Rs 15,000 a year per college for a placement-cell dashboard and bulk checks.
Rs 4,999 a month for employers to publish a verified recruiter page.
Pricing is a suggestion and has not been validated.
risk: Candidates may not bother checking an offer that looks exciting, which is exactly when they are most vulnerable.
test: Give a free WhatsApp check number to two college placement cells for two weeks and count how many students forward an offer without being reminded. A reasonable bar: 100 checks from about 500 students. If use is low, pivot to selling the check to placement cells and HR teams, who will run it for candidates.
caution: Do not call a named company a scam publicly; show reasons and confidence instead. Uploaded offers contain personal data, so get consent, keep them briefly and follow India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
sources: CXOToday: Indeed report on job scams in India
Business Today: More than 9 in 10 job seekers encounter fake job offers
People Matters: 82% of Indian professionals check jobs for scams (LinkedIn)
The Week: Job applications used to recruit money mules
Free Press Journal: Mumbai woman loses Rs 11.28 lakh to fake job offer
take: I see fake offers shared in professional groups every week, and the people who fall for them are usually first-time job seekers in a hurry. Claude can explain why an offer looks suspicious in plain language, which matters more than a bare score. The hard part is reach: the tool has to be one forward away, inside the apps where these offers arrive.
